editor_note: I found no misleading drift. Constraints, penalties, the warm-start chains, the benchmark notes and the MIS/Max-k-Cut explanations all keep their meaning. "Constrained" is translated two ways: as "optimasi biner terbatas" in [0] and [7], which can read as "limited binary optimization", and as "dengan batasan" everywhere else ([12], [23], [34]). The graph-coloring terms "Pewarnaan graf 3" ([52]) and "pewarnaan 3" ([53]) are awkward calques; the usual forms are "pewarnaan-3 graf" and "pewarnaan-3". "Pemfiksasian variabel" ([28]) is also stiff.

examples.source: Solve constrained binary optimization problems
examples.translation: Selesaikan masalah optimasi biner terbatas
examples.suggested: Selesaikan masalah optimasi biner dengan batasan
examples.why: 'terbatas' reads as 'limited/bounded'. The rest of the file uses 'dengan batasan', so the term is inconsistent.

examples.source: Graph 3-coloring (Max-3-Cut)
examples.translation: Pewarnaan graf 3 (Max-3-Cut)
examples.suggested: Pewarnaan-3 graf (Max-3-Cut)
examples.why: The current wording reads as 'coloring of graph 3' rather than 3-coloring of a graph. [53] has the same problem ('pewarnaan 3').

examples.source: reflects variable fixing in preprocessing
examples.translation: mencerminkan pemfiksasian variabel dalam preprocessing
examples.suggested: mencerminkan penetapan nilai variabel pada tahap preprocessing
examples.why: 'pemfiksasian' is a stiff coinage. 'penetapan nilai variabel' is more natural.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (7, 9, 13, 22) would mislead a learner. The meaning matches the English in each: the caveat that one setting can help one circuit and hurt another is kept, 0 (lowest) against 3 (highest) is correct, and the reasons for the improvements (fewer gates, dynamical decoupling) are right. The only problems are two calques in entry 9. "untuk dicoba dioptimalkan oleh Transpiler" stacks passives awkwardly, and "apa yang kamu harapkan untuk diukur" copies the English "what you'd expect to measure" word for word. A native editor would rewrite both.

examples.source: what you'd expect to measure if you ran this on a perfect quantum computer an infinite number of times
examples.translation: apa yang kamu harapkan untuk diukur jika kamu menjalankan ini pada komputer kuantum sempurna sebanyak tak terhingga kali
examples.suggested: hasil pengukuran yang kamu harapkan jika menjalankannya tak terhingga kali pada komputer kuantum sempurna
examples.why: Copies the English 'expect to measure' word for word, and 'sebanyak tak terhingga kali' reads awkwardly. Indonesian technical writing would name the outcome ('hasil pengukuran') instead.

examples.source: Create a small circuit for the transpiler to try to optimize.
examples.translation: Buat Circuit kecil untuk dicoba dioptimalkan oleh Transpiler.
examples.suggested: Buat Circuit kecil yang akan coba dioptimalkan oleh Transpiler.
examples.why: The stacked passive 'untuk dicoba dioptimalkan' reads stiffly. A relative clause with 'yang akan coba' is more natural and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries (7, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19) changes the meaning. The three plugin kinds, the input/output descriptions, the unique-name and reserved-name rules and the reserved-names table all match the English. The one fix is a terminology split in entry 7. The third bullet calls the plugin 'Plugin sintesis tingkat tinggi' but the thing it synthesizes 'objek high-level' (twice, plus 'Objek high-level direpresentasikan...'). Entries 12 and 17 and the rest of the page (e.g. entry 48, 'objek "tingkat tinggi"') use 'tingkat tinggi', so entry 7 should be changed to match.

examples.source: takes as input a "high-level object" such as a Clifford operator ... implementing that high-level object. High-level objects are represented by subclasses
examples.translation: menerima input berupa "objek high-level" seperti operator Clifford ... mengimplementasikan objek high-level tersebut. Objek high-level direpresentasikan oleh subkelas
examples.suggested: menerima input berupa "objek tingkat tinggi" seperti operator Clifford ... mengimplementasikan objek tingkat tinggi tersebut. Objek tingkat tinggi direpresentasikan oleh subkelas
examples.why: The same bullet translates 'high-level' as 'tingkat tinggi' in the plugin name but leaves it in English for the object. Entries 12, 17 and 48 use 'tingkat tinggi', so this bullet is the odd one out.

editor_note: Entry 15 is accurate. It keeps exclusive access ("akses eksklusif ke sistem"), keeps calibration jobs excluded ("termasuk job kalibrasi") and correctly says the cost function runs on the user's local machine. There is no drift and nothing made up. Two phrases read like literal translation from English. "komunikasi sering" puts the adjective after the noun awkwardly and should be "komunikasi yang sering". The sentence opening "Menggunakan Session membantu ..." copies the English -ing subject and reads more naturally as "Penggunaan Session membantu ...". "secara lebih terprediksi" is also a little stiff.

examples.source: iterative tasks that require frequent communication between classical and quantum resources
examples.translation: tugas iteratif yang memerlukan komunikasi sering antara sumber daya klasik dan kuantum
examples.suggested: tugas iteratif yang memerlukan komunikasi yang sering antara sumber daya klasik dan kuantum
examples.why: Putting 'sering' straight after the noun with no 'yang' sounds like literal translation. Indonesian technical writers would add 'yang' here or write 'komunikasi intensif'.

examples.source: Using sessions helps avoid delays caused by queuing each job separately
examples.translation: Menggunakan Session membantu menghindari penundaan yang disebabkan oleh antrean setiap job secara terpisah
examples.suggested: Penggunaan Session membantu menghindari penundaan akibat setiap job harus mengantre secara terpisah
examples.why: Starting the sentence with the verb 'Menggunakan' as its subject copies the English gerund. A noun ('Penggunaan') is the natural subject in Indonesian, and 'akibat ... mengantre' is smoother than the passive 'yang disebabkan oleh antrean'.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 12 is faithful and natural: "Dalam makalah ini kami menggunakan `ibmq_vigo`, salah satu prosesor IBM Quantum Canary" keeps the example matched to the citation guidance in entry 11 and correctly leaves the product name "IBM Quantum Canary" untranslated.

Both rewritten entries are faithful: in [9], "by up to a factor of two" becomes "hingga setengahnya", which keeps the "up to" limit and the halving, and in [28], "error-suppressed" becomes "sehingga error-nya lebih rendah", which keeps the cause-and-effect link without overstating it.

Entries 23 and 55 are faithful and natural. "Perilaku lama Qiskit" and "akan diselesaikan pada rilis Qiskit mendatang" carry the legacy caveat and the future-fix promise intact. Entry 29 keeps the right condition (a mismatch in either the parameter count or the qubit count raises QASM2ParseError), but it says so awkwardly with "tidak cocok sekaligus (salah satu saja sudah cukup)". On a first read, "tidak cocok sekaligus" suggests both counts must mismatch. The parenthetical then has to correct that, and it is an added gloss that is not in the source. A plain "atau" states the condition directly and cannot be misread.

examples.source: but does not match both the number of parameters and the number of qubits, the importer will raise a QASM2ParseError
examples.translation: tapi jumlah parameter dan jumlah qubitnya tidak cocok sekaligus (salah satu saja sudah cukup), importer akan memunculkan QASM2ParseError
examples.suggested: tetapi jumlah parameter atau jumlah qubit-nya tidak cocok, importer akan memunculkan QASM2ParseError
examples.why: The meaning comes through, but only because an inserted parenthetical corrects a clause that first reads as 'both must mismatch'. That makes the sentence stiff and ambiguous, and using 'atau' says it cleanly.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 3 keeps "salah satu cara berikut" and SSO/IDP as they are, entry 7 renders dynamic rules as "aturan dinamis" and keeps "secara manual saat mereka bergabung", and entry 9 uses "Lihat" for each bullet with no meaning lost.

The five rewritten entries (19, 71, 74, 89, 101) keep the English meaning, including "Executor tidak memiliki error suppression atau mitigasi bawaan", the meas_level="both" caveat and the table row "Batalkan twirling pengukuran / Otomatis"; the only loose end is that untouched entries 64 and 93 say "twirling measurement" and "measurement twirling" where entry 89 says "twirling pengukuran".

Entry 19 is faithful: the caveat about the tuple order is kept intact ("output dikembalikan sebagai tuple `(input_dim, output_dim)`, yang merupakan kebalikan dari bentuk matriks yang mendasarinya"), and it uses the same wording as entry 18 ("kamu bisa menggunakan properti", "yang mendasarinya").

Entry 24 keeps the English meaning. "Can depend", "in some cases", "might achieve similar" and the "therefore consider the complete workflow" caveat all carry over, so it would not mislead a learner. Two small slips remain. The rewrite uses "alur kerja optimisasi", but everywhere else the page writes "optimasi" (optimasi kombinatorial, Optimasi tidak terkendali/terkendali, optimasi skala utilitas), so this one spelling breaks the file's convention. Also, "bergantung pada baik instance masalah maupun ..." copies the English "both ... and" word order and reads stiffly. A native editor would write "baik pada ... maupun pada ...".

examples.source: Evaluation should therefore consider the complete optimization workflow.
examples.translation: Oleh karena itu, evaluasi harus mempertimbangkan keseluruhan alur kerja optimisasi.
examples.suggested: Oleh karena itu, evaluasi harus mempertimbangkan keseluruhan alur kerja optimasi.
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'optimasi' for this term. 'optimisasi' is the only other spelling on the page, so it should be changed to match.

examples.source: Performance can depend on both the problem instance and subsequent processing steps.
examples.translation: Performa dapat bergantung pada baik instance masalah maupun langkah-langkah pemrosesan selanjutnya.
examples.suggested: Performa dapat bergantung baik pada instance masalah maupun pada langkah-langkah pemrosesan selanjutnya.
examples.why: Putting 'baik' after the preposition 'pada' copies the English 'on both ... and' order. Natural Indonesian puts 'baik' before the preposition and repeats it: 'baik pada ... maupun pada'.

editor_note: Entry 3 is faithful and natural: "memang memutus kompatibilitas dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya" keeps the emphatic "does break" and the full "all previous versions" scope, and "environment" matches its use in entry 4.

Entry 141's benchmark table is faithful: every score, version and row is unchanged, the headers read naturally ("Metrik Benchmark", "Tanggal rilis", "Dilatih pada versi Qiskit"), and the month names are localized correctly (Januari 2026, Juni 2025, Februari 2025).

The three rewritten entries match their English: entry 96 keeps the init-error vs prob_meas1_prep0 distinction ("pengukuran gabungan dari error inisialisasi dan prosedur membedakan ...", "Dalam batas pengukuran sempurna, kedua kuantitas ini sama"), and entries 60 and 101 translate only the table labels ("Lihat dengan Qiskit", "Waktu dephasing", "CLOPS (atau CLOPS_h)") and leave the code and UI names unchanged.

All 13 rewritten entries match the English, including the shots-precedence logic in [12] and [17] ("menimpa nilai apa pun yang diatur untuk `default_shots` pada run saat ini", "nilai shots dari opsi yang akan digunakan, terutama `default_shots`"), and the "Dokumentasi API `…`" link labels are used the same way throughout.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, so neither would mislead a learner. Entry 17 ("mengharuskan kamu menempatkan file `.py` workload-mu di dalam direktori tersendiri") reads naturally. Entry 15 copies the English sentence structure: "…menambahkan kode ke dalamnya yang, saat kamu unggah ke Qiskit Serverless, akan mentranspilasi…" puts a relative "yang" after "ke dalamnya", then breaks it with a comma clause. That leaves it unclear whether the file or the code does the transpiling, and a native editor would split the sentence.

examples.source: This example walks you through creating and adding to a program file that, when you upload it to Qiskit Serverless, will transpile a `circuit` against a given `backend` and target `optimization_level`.
examples.translation: Contoh ini memandumu membuat sebuah file program dan menambahkan kode ke dalamnya yang, saat kamu unggah ke Qiskit Serverless, akan mentranspilasi sebuah `circuit` untuk `backend` tertentu dan `optimization_level` target yang kamu tentukan.
examples.suggested: Contoh ini memandumu membuat sebuah file program lalu mengisinya dengan kode. Setelah kamu unggah ke Qiskit Serverless, program ini akan mentranspilasi sebuah `circuit` untuk `backend` tertentu dengan `optimization_level` target yang kamu tentukan.
examples.why: The comma-interrupted relative clause after 'ke dalamnya yang' copies English syntax and makes it unclear what 'yang' refers to. Splitting the sentence reads natively and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (11, 31, 33, 40, 47) keep the English meaning, and none would mislead a learner. The "harus" emphasis in [33] and the parametrized vs. non-parametrized caveat in [11] and [31] are intact. Entry [40] uses the non-standard verb "mengorganisir" (KBBI prefers "mengorganisasi"; "mengelompokkan" reads more naturally here). The same sentence also mixes "Circuit input mereka" with "sirkuit dinamis", and [33] uses "sirkuit" while [11], [31] and [47] use "Circuit". That split should go away once the separate term sweep standardizes the circuit term.

examples.source: The Sampler result objects organize data in terms of their input circuits' classical register names
examples.translation: Objek hasil Sampler mengorganisir data berdasarkan nama register klasik dari Circuit input mereka
examples.suggested: Objek hasil Sampler mengelompokkan data berdasarkan nama register klasik dari sirkuit input-nya
examples.why: 'mengorganisir' is a non-standard form (KBBI: mengorganisasi). 'mengelompokkan' is more natural, and '-nya' reads better than 'mereka' for inanimate objects.

examples.source: their input circuits' classical register names, for compatibility with dynamic circuits
examples.translation: dari Circuit input mereka, untuk kompatibilitas dengan sirkuit dinamis
examples.suggested: dari sirkuit input-nya, untuk kompatibilitas dengan sirkuit dinamis
examples.why: One sentence renders 'circuit' two ways, and [33] also uses 'sirkuit' while [11], [31] and [47] use 'Circuit'. This is only an inconsistency and does not mislead.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (9, 15, 20) changes the meaning. Entry 9 keeps the orchestra analogy intact: StagedPassManager is the conductor, the PassManagers are the instrument sections ("bagian instrumen") and each Pass is a musician. Entry 20 translates "hardware-aware" accurately as "yang memperhitungkan karakteristik hardware". One style issue remains in entry 15: "gerbang single-Qubit dan two-Qubit" and "gerbang multi-Qubit" keep the English modifiers "single-" and "two-" inside Indonesian noun phrases, and the calque "mengonversi sirkuit ke semua gerbang" sounds stiff. A native editor would write "gerbang satu-qubit dan dua-qubit".

examples.source: converting the circuit to all single- and two-qubit gates
examples.translation: mengonversi sirkuit ke semua gerbang single-Qubit dan two-Qubit
examples.suggested: mengonversi sirkuit sehingga hanya berisi gerbang satu-qubit dan dua-qubit
examples.why: The English modifiers 'single-'/'two-' are left inside an Indonesian noun phrase, and 'ke semua gerbang' copies the English word order. The meaning is correct, but a native technical writer would put it differently.

editor_note: Entry 7 renders the heading "Plot histogram" as "Gambar histogram". It does not mislead. Still, "Gambar" in a bare heading most naturally reads as the noun ("Histogram image") rather than the action "plot a histogram". It also breaks the pattern of the page's other plotting headings: [0] uses "Plot hasil…", [13] "saat plotting histogram" and [22] "Plotting hasil Estimator". Use "Plotting histogram" to match [22], or the clearly verbal "Menggambar histogram".

examples.source: Plot histogram {#plot-histogram}
examples.translation: Gambar histogram {#plot-histogram}
examples.suggested: Plotting histogram {#plot-histogram}
examples.why: As a heading, 'Gambar histogram' reads as the noun 'histogram image' rather than the action. It is also inconsistent with the sibling heading [22] 'Plotting hasil Estimator' and with 'plotting' in [13].

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 5 keeps the Holevo claim exactly: without shared entanglement, one qubit carries at most one bit. It also keeps the caveat that the theorem is more general, and the *penggandaan* (doubling) emphasis. Entry 21 is faithful. Two small fixes remain. Entry 5 spells 'mengkomunikasikan', but standard KBBI spelling is 'mengomunikasikan' (the k merges into the prefix). Entry 9 turns 'In words' into 'Secara ringkas' ('in brief'), which loses the point that this is the prose version of the circuit diagram.

examples.source: it is impossible to communicate more than one bit of classical information by sending a single qubit
examples.translation: tidak mungkin untuk mengkomunikasikan lebih dari satu bit informasi klasik
examples.suggested: tidak mungkin mengomunikasikan lebih dari satu bit informasi klasik
examples.why: Standard KBBI spelling merges the k ('mengomunikasikan'). The 'untuk' after 'tidak mungkin' is also a calque of the English and can be dropped.

examples.source: In words, here is what Alice does:
examples.translation: Secara ringkas, inilah yang Alice lakukan:
examples.suggested: Jika diuraikan dengan kata-kata, inilah yang dilakukan Alice:
examples.why: 'Secara ringkas' means 'in brief'. The English contrasts a prose description with the circuit diagram above it, and this rendering loses that contrast. It is a small shift that does not mislead.

editor_note: Entry 5 is faithful and natural, and it uses the standard terms: inner products→"hasil kali dalam", projective measurements→"pengukuran proyektif", no-cloning theorem→"teorema no-cloning". It also keeps the "tidak ortogonal" condition intact in "ketidakmungkinan untuk membedakan dengan sempurna".

All three rewritten entries (12, 21, 22) keep the meaning of the English. Entry 21 is accurate: "logis/fisik", "tidak pernah terekspos" and the caveat that the number of physical qubits "bisa berbeda" all come through. In entry 22, "sesering mungkin" ("as often as possible") slightly overstates "frequently", and "pekerjaan konstan diperlukan" is a calque of "constant work is required". In entry 12, the opening "Sekarang" is a literal copy of the English discourse marker "Now", and "Nobody suggests otherwise!" works better as a concession than as "Tidak ada yang membantah hal itu!".

examples.source: It is critically important that this is done both frequently and in parallel.
examples.translation: Sangat penting agar koreksi ini dilakukan sesering mungkin dan secara paralel.
examples.suggested: Sangat penting agar koreksi ini dilakukan secara sering sekaligus paralel.
examples.why: 'sesering mungkin' means 'as often as possible', which is stronger than 'frequently'. The shift is small and does not mislead.

examples.source: constant work is required to remove it from the system
examples.translation: pekerjaan konstan diperlukan untuk mengeluarkannya dari sistem
examples.suggested: diperlukan upaya terus-menerus untuk membuangnya dari sistem
examples.why: 'pekerjaan konstan' is a literal calque. 'upaya terus-menerus' is how a native technical writer would put it.

examples.source: Now, it is certainly reasonable to object ... Nobody suggests otherwise!
examples.translation: Sekarang, sangat wajar untuk mengajukan keberatan ... Tidak ada yang membantah hal itu!
examples.suggested: Tentu saja wajar untuk mengajukan keberatan ... Memang benar demikian!
examples.why: 'Sekarang' copies the English discourse 'Now' word for word and reads as a time marker. 'Tidak ada yang membantah' is a stiff way to render the author's concession.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (4, 5, 7, 12) say what the English says. The survey note, the exam navigation and the Credly privacy notice keep every caveat: the US-based processor, the shared fields, and sharing with subsidiaries and third parties. The remaining problems are phrasing. Entry 5 calques "content offering" as "penawaran konten", which reads like marketing MT. Entry 7 half-translates "badging exam" as "ujian badging". Entry 12 has a clumsy doubled "untuk ... untukmu" and a vague "Hal ini" standing in for the personal information. The rewrites also use "kamu/-mu" while the untouched entries 8-9 next to them use "Anda". Both registers are allowed, but mixing them on one short page is noticeable.

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Masukanmu akan digunakan untuk meningkatkan penawaran konten dan pengalaman pengguna kami.
examples.suggested: Masukanmu akan kami gunakan untuk menyempurnakan konten dan pengalaman pengguna kami.
examples.why: 'penawaran konten' is a literal calque of 'content offering'; a native writer would just say 'konten' or 'materi'.

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.translation: dan mengikuti ujian badging untuk Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.suggested: dan mengikuti ujian untuk memperoleh badge Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.why: 'ujian badging' leaves an English gerund inside Indonesian syntax. 'ujian untuk memperoleh badge' is clearer and matches the 'badge' used elsewhere on the page.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge, ... It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Untuk menerbitkan IBM Digital Badge untukmu, ... Hal ini akan ditangani dengan cara yang konsisten dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Agar IBM Digital Badge dapat diterbitkan untukmu, ... Informasi tersebut akan ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM.
examples.why: The doubled 'Untuk ... untukmu' is clumsy. 'Hal ini' is vague about what is being handled, and 'dengan cara yang konsisten dengan' is a calque.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (3, 5, 6) keep the English meaning. The Shor tooltip keeps both dates (1994 conference paper, 1997 journal paper), 'estimasi fase' and 'transformasi Fourier kuantum' are used consistently, and entry 6 ('Berbekal itu, John beralih ke algoritma Shor') is natural. Two phrasings would still be smoothed by an editor. Entry 5 copies the English word order in 'memandu Anda melalui konten pada pelajaran ini tentang estimasi fase kuantum'. In entry 3 the tooltip clause 'masalah yang berbeda tapi terkait yaitu menghitung logaritma diskrit' is missing a comma before 'yaitu' and would read better with 'tetapi berkaitan'. The 'Circuit kuantum' leak in entry 3 is left to the deterministic sweep.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson on quantum phase estimation
examples.translation: John Watrous memandu Anda melalui konten pada pelajaran ini tentang estimasi fase kuantum
examples.suggested: John Watrous memandu Anda memahami materi pelajaran tentang estimasi fase kuantum ini
examples.why: This copies the English order ('konten pada pelajaran ini tentang ...'), which reads stiffly. 'Materi pelajaran' is the usual Indonesian phrase for teaching content.

examples.source: the different but related problem of computing discrete logarithms
examples.translation: masalah yang berbeda tapi terkait yaitu menghitung logaritma diskrit
examples.suggested: masalah yang berbeda tetapi berkaitan, yaitu menghitung logaritma diskrit
examples.why: Without a comma before 'yaitu' the sentence runs on, and 'tapi' is a bit casual for a written tooltip. The meaning is correct.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (5, 7, 12) would mislead a learner. The 16-of-20 pass rule is in entry 8, which was not rewritten. The Credly data-sharing notice in entry 12 keeps all its details: the data shared (name, email, badge), the purposes, and sharing with subsidiaries and third parties worldwide. There are two small polish issues. Entry 7 translates "badging exam" as "ujian lencana (badging)", and the English word in brackets reads like a translator's note, not natural Indonesian. Entry 12 moves the final period inside the link text ("[di sini.]"), where the source has it outside the link.

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for General formulation of quantum information
examples.translation: tempat kamu bisa mengikuti ujian lencana (badging) untuk Formulasi umum informasi kuantum
examples.suggested: tempat kamu bisa mengikuti ujian untuk memperoleh lencana Formulasi umum informasi kuantum
examples.why: The English word "(badging)" in brackets is a translator's crutch. "ujian untuk memperoleh lencana" says the same thing in natural Indonesian.

examples.source: The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed [here](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.translation: Pernyataan Privasi IBM bisa dilihat [di sini.](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/)
examples.suggested: Pernyataan Privasi IBM bisa dilihat [di sini](https://www.ibm.com/privacy/us/).
examples.why: The sentence-final period has moved inside the link text. It should stay outside the link, as in the source.

editor_note: Entry 21 carries every clause of the Credly notice over faithfully, including "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diotorisasi oleh IBM", the permissive "IBM dapat membagikan … secara global" and "ditangani sesuai dengan praktik privasi IBM", and it uses the Anda register with nothing softened or dropped.

All four rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally, including "100 qubit atau lebih" in [4], "kami menyarankan Anda sudah familier dengan informasi kuantum dan sirkuit kuantum" in [6], and the Credly notice in [16], which keeps every data-sharing caveat ("anak perusahaan IBM dan pihak ketiga secara global").

None of the 8 rewritten entries would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix several calques. In [83], "don't scale very well" became "tidak berkembang dengan sangat baik" ("doesn't develop very well"), which loses the scaling idea, and "Gate Pauli sebaliknya yang dibangun" and "cara ini untuk membatalkan noise" read stiffly. In [80], "less and less noise" is copied word for word as "lebih sedikit dan lebih sedikit noise". In [54], "tingkat kesalahan perkiraan" can be misread as "estimation error rate", and "dengan tangan" would read better as "secara manual". [81] drops the hedge in "can end up being".

examples.source: because the required computational resources don't scale very well compared to the other error mitigation techniques
examples.translation: karena sumber daya komputasi yang diperlukan tidak berkembang dengan sangat baik dibandingkan dengan teknik mitigasi kesalahan lainnya
examples.suggested: karena kebutuhan sumber daya komputasinya tidak berskala sebaik teknik mitigasi kesalahan lainnya
examples.why: 'berkembang' means grow or develop, so the idea of computational scaling (cost growing with problem size) is lost.

examples.source: to predict what the results would look like if there were less and less noise
examples.translation: untuk memprediksi seperti apa hasilnya jika ada lebih sedikit dan lebih sedikit noise
examples.suggested: untuk memprediksi seperti apa hasilnya jika noise-nya semakin berkurang
examples.why: 'less and less' is copied word for word. Indonesian says this with 'semakin'.

examples.source: You can do it by hand ... based on approximate error rates. The transpiler ... can also make an informed suggestion.
examples.translation: Kamu bisa melakukannya dengan tangan ... berdasarkan tingkat kesalahan perkiraan. Transpiler ... juga bisa memberikan saran berdasarkan informasi tersebut.
examples.suggested: Kamu bisa melakukannya secara manual ... berdasarkan perkiraan tingkat kesalahan. Transpiler ... juga bisa memberikan saran yang terinformasi.
examples.why: 'tingkat kesalahan perkiraan' reads as 'estimation error rate' rather than 'approximate error rates'. 'dengan tangan' is too literal, and 'berdasarkan informasi tersebut' ties the suggestion to a specific antecedent the English does not have.

examples.source: so that they effectively have the opposite Pauli gates built in ... However, this way of undoing the noise is very costly
examples.translation: sehingga mereka secara efektif memiliki Gate Pauli sebaliknya yang dibangun ... Namun, cara ini untuk membatalkan noise sangat mahal
examples.suggested: sehingga secara efektif di dalamnya tertanam Gate Pauli kebalikannya ... Namun, cara membatalkan noise seperti ini sangat mahal
examples.why: Stiff word order copied from English, and 'sebaliknya yang dibangun' is awkward.

examples.source: so you can see how it can end up being computationally expensive
examples.translation: jadi kamu bisa melihat betapa mahalnya secara komputasi
examples.suggested: jadi kamu bisa melihat bagaimana hal ini pada akhirnya bisa menjadi mahal secara komputasi
examples.why: The hedge 'can end up being' is dropped, which turns a possibility into a flat claim. The shift is small but real.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful and reads naturally. It renders "badging exam" as "ujian lencana", which matches "lencana" in entries 0 and 2. Entry 12 is faithful overall, but "kepada anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga IBM secara global" puts "IBM" after "pihak ketiga", so it reads as "IBM's third parties". The English means IBM subsidiaries and third parties in general, so the fix is to reorder to "anak perusahaan IBM dan pihak ketiga di seluruh dunia". The rest of the privacy notice keeps the "kamu/-mu" register and every caveat, so nothing in it misleads a reader.

examples.source: IBM may share the personal information collected with IBM subsidiaries and third parties globally.
examples.translation: IBM dapat membagikan informasi pribadi yang dikumpulkan kepada anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga IBM secara global.
examples.suggested: IBM dapat membagikan informasi pribadi yang dikumpulkan kepada anak perusahaan IBM dan pihak ketiga di seluruh dunia.
examples.why: With 'IBM' at the end, the phrase reads as 'IBM's third parties'. The English means IBM's subsidiaries and outside third parties, and 'di seluruh dunia' sounds more natural than the calque 'secara global'.

editor_note: None of the nine rewritten entries changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The caveats come through intact: 100% accuracy is "sangat berbeda dari keunggulan kuantum" in [76], and a depth over 100 is "sudah tidak layak dipakai" in [82]. Entry [91] renders "does not scale like the number of features" as "tidak berkembang seperti jumlah fitur". That is a calque and reads oddly for a claim about computing cost. Entry [76] renders "running time" as "waktu berjalan" where "waktu eksekusi" is the usual term, and [70] drops the object in "jika kita menjalankan pada komputer kuantum nyata".

examples.source: does not scale like the number of features or qubits
examples.translation: tidak berkembang seperti jumlah fitur atau qubit
examples.suggested: tidak bertambah seiring dengan jumlah fitur atau qubit
examples.why: 'berkembang seperti' is a literal rendering of 'scale like'. It is unclear as a statement about how computing cost grows.

examples.source: How are the accuracy and running time affected
examples.translation: Bagaimana akurasi dan waktu berjalan dipengaruhi
examples.suggested: Bagaimana akurasi dan waktu eksekusi dipengaruhi
examples.why: 'waktu berjalan' is a word-for-word calque. 'waktu eksekusi' (or 'waktu komputasi') is the conventional term.

examples.source: if we were running on a real quantum computer in this example
examples.translation: jika kita menjalankan pada komputer kuantum nyata dalam contoh ini
examples.suggested: jika kita menjalankannya pada komputer kuantum nyata dalam contoh ini
examples.why: The transitive verb 'menjalankan' has no object, so the sentence reads as incomplete.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (5, 7, 12) keep the English meaning, including "intended to be taken after" as "sebaiknya diikuti setelah", the full list of Credly-shared data "(nama, alamat email, dan lencana yang diperoleh)", and the caveat about sharing with "anak perusahaan IBM dan pihak ketiga secara global"; they use informal "kamu" throughout.

The 12 rewritten entries are faithful, and 'ber-noise', 'Sampler ber-noise' and 'model noise' are used consistently across entries 12-30. Entry 33 turns the neutral 'see how the error scales with respect to the number of time steps' into 'melihat bagaimana error meningkat seiring bertambahnya jumlah langkah waktu' ('how the error increases'). That states the result before the experiment is run, but it matches what the lesson goes on to show, so it is a minor defect. Entry 33 also calques 'consider' as 'mempertimbangkan'; entry 18 already uses the more natural 'Kita tinjau'. Entry 28's '25x jumlah shots' reads stiffly.

examples.source: see how the error scales with respect to the number of time steps
examples.translation: melihat bagaimana error meningkat seiring bertambahnya jumlah langkah waktu
examples.suggested: melihat bagaimana error berubah terhadap jumlah langkah waktu
examples.why: 'Scales' is neutral, but 'meningkat' says the error increases, stating the outcome before the experiment. Minor, because the lesson's results support it.

examples.source: We consider 6-qubit Trotterized circuits
examples.translation: Kita mempertimbangkan Circuit Trotterisasi 6-Qubit
examples.suggested: Kita tinjau Circuit Trotterisasi 6-Qubit
examples.why: 'Mempertimbangkan' means to weigh or deliberate, so it is a calque of 'consider'. Entry 18 already uses the idiomatic 'Kita tinjau'.

examples.source: Try 25x number of shots (= 10_000 shots)
examples.translation: Coba 25x jumlah shots (= 10_000 shots)
examples.suggested: Coba jumlah shots 25 kali lipat (= 10_000 shots)
examples.why: '25x jumlah shots' copies the English word order. '25 kali lipat' is how Indonesian technical prose expresses a multiplier.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 16, "2.2 Peta coupling", keeps the meaning, but it doesn't match the section's own body. Entry 17, directly below it, keeps the term fully in English: "Kita sekarang menggambar coupling map dari perangkat". So the heading translates half the term and the body keeps all of it in English. A learner will still recognise the concept, so this is not misleading. It is still a within-file inconsistency that a native editor would fix, and the simplest fix is to make the heading "2.2 Coupling map" to match the body and Qiskit's CouplingMap.

examples.source: 2.2 Coupling map {#22-coupling-map}
examples.translation: 2.2 Peta coupling {#22-coupling-map}
examples.suggested: 2.2 Coupling map {#22-coupling-map}
examples.why: The heading translates half the term, but the section body (entry 17) keeps it as 'coupling map'. This is inconsistent within one section. Keeping the English term matches the body and the Qiskit API name.

editor_note: All 8 rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Nothing is inverted or dropped: entry 98 still says one result `001` with certainty, decimal `1`, divided by $2^n$. Entry 93 uses the English word "state" ("mengonversi state dari register pencacah"), but everywhere else the page translates "state" as "keadaan" (entries 19, 27, 34, 51, 53, 55), so this one entry breaks the page's term convention. Entries 89 ("gate Hadamard pada qubit pencacah") and 91 ("operasi uniter terkontrol") are defensible, fit the "register pencacah" and "gate $T$" usage already on the page, and are not counted as defects.

examples.source: We apply the inverse quantum Fourier transformation to convert the state of the counting register, then measure the counting register:
examples.translation: Kita menerapkan transformasi Fourier kuantum invers untuk mengonversi state dari register pencacah, kemudian mengukur register pencacah:
examples.suggested: Kita menerapkan transformasi Fourier kuantum invers untuk mengubah keadaan register pencacah, kemudian mengukur register pencacah:
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page "state" is "keadaan". Keeping the English "state" only here is inconsistent, and "mengonversi ... dari" reads like a word-for-word calque of the English.

editor_note: The meaning of all 8 rewritten entries holds: the no-FTL answer (110), the teleportation-vs-superdense contrast (113) and the marginalization in 105 are all correct, so nothing here would mislead a learner. In entry 53, "a shared entangled state" became "state terkait (entangled) yang sama", which reads as "the same entangled state" rather than one the two parties share; "bersama" or "yang dibagikan" would fix that. The rewrites also render entanglement as "terkait"/"keterkaitan" (53, 113, 115), a weak everyday word meaning "related". The rest of the page uses "belitan" (11) and "terjerat" (55), so the concept now has three names. Entry 113 opens with the calque "Hampir pengaturan yang sama"; the natural order is "Pengaturan yang hampir sama".

examples.source: a shared entangled state, like the Bell state
examples.translation: state terkait (entangled) yang sama, seperti Bell state
examples.suggested: state terbelit (entangled) yang dimiliki bersama, seperti Bell state
examples.why: 'yang sama' means 'the same', not 'shared'. Also, 'terkait' ('related') is a weak rendering of entangled, and it clashes with 'belitan' (entry 11) and 'terjerat' (entry 55) elsewhere in the file.

examples.source: Almost the same setup can be used for a different purpose.
examples.translation: Hampir pengaturan yang sama bisa digunakan untuk tujuan yang berbeda.
examples.suggested: Pengaturan yang hampir sama bisa digunakan untuk tujuan yang berbeda.
examples.why: The word order is copied from English. In natural Indonesian, 'hampir' goes right before 'sama'.

examples.source: Alice and Bob share an entangled pair (e-bit)
examples.translation: Alice dan Bob berbagi pasangan terkait (e-bit)
examples.suggested: Alice dan Bob berbagi pasangan terbelit (e-bit)
examples.why: 'terkait' is not the conventional Indonesian physics term for entangled, and entanglement already appears on this page under 'belitan' and 'terjerat'.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries misleads: the Trotterization description, the note that Pauli terms may or may not commute (berkomutasi), and the Lie–Trotter approximation all keep the English meaning. Entry 15 has two calques. "pada waktu berikutnya" means "at the next time", which hints at a discrete next step rather than an arbitrary later time t. "Diberikan sebuah keadaan" copies the English "Given a state". In entry 17, "Hamiltonian yang menarik" is a literal rendering of "Hamiltonians of interest". Entry 49 uses the Indonesian "sirkuit", while the rest of the page uses "Circuit"/"circuit", so the term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Given a state at time $t=0$, how do we obtain the system's state at a later time $|\psi(t)\rangle$
examples.translation: Diberikan sebuah keadaan pada waktu $t=0$, bagaimana kita memperoleh keadaan sistem pada waktu berikutnya $|\psi(t)\rangle$
examples.suggested: Jika keadaan pada waktu $t=0$ diketahui, bagaimana kita memperoleh keadaan sistem pada waktu kemudian $|\psi(t)\rangle$
examples.why: 'Diberikan ...' is a calque of 'Given ...'. 'waktu berikutnya' reads as 'the next time (step)' rather than 'a later time t'.

examples.source: Most Hamiltonians of interest will not have just a single term
examples.translation: Sebagian besar Hamiltonian yang menarik tidak akan hanya memiliki satu suku
examples.suggested: Sebagian besar Hamiltonian yang ingin kita kaji tidak hanya memiliki satu suku
examples.why: 'yang menarik' is a literal rendering of 'of interest'. It reads as 'interesting/attractive' rather than 'relevant to study'.

examples.source: We here construct a circuit for a single time step using Lie–Trotter.
examples.translation: Di sini kita membangun sebuah sirkuit untuk satu langkah waktu menggunakan Lie–Trotter.
examples.suggested: Match the term used in the rest of the page (circuit/sirkuit) once the separate term-leak sweep has run.
examples.why: 'sirkuit' here while the surrounding entries use 'Circuit'/'circuit', so the term is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural. Entry 7 renders the course name as "Desain algoritma variasional", which matches the title, and entry 12 keeps every clause of the privacy notice: Credly as the "prosesor data pihak ketiga" located in "Amerika Serikat", the three shared data items, and global sharing with "anak perusahaan dan pihak ketiga". Both use the informal "kamu"/"-mu" register.

Entry 64 is faithful and uses the same terms as the rest of the page: it keeps both circuits ("sirkuit yang dioptimalkan AQC dan sirkuit Trotter baseline"), and its "backend palsu", "primitif" and "observabel ZZ" match entries 62 and 41.

The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. Frustration, the extensive-energy scaling caveat, the ground state as an NP-hard problem and the transpile_only/shots option semantics all come through intact, and the "Anda" register holds. A native editor would still polish three phrasings in the physics background and the options sentence. In [11], "rugged" becomes "bergelombang" (wavy), which undersells the many-minima picture, and "perilaku glassy" leaves a bare English adjective inside Indonesian prose. In [37], "gunakan options" keeps the English plural noun awkwardly.

examples.source: a highly complex, "rugged", energy landscape
examples.translation: lanskap energi yang sangat kompleks, "bergelombang"
examples.suggested: lanskap energi yang sangat kompleks dan "terjal" (berbukit-bukit)
examples.why: 'Bergelombang' suggests smooth waves; the rugged landscape of spin glasses is jagged with many local minima, which 'terjal'/'kasar' conveys better.

examples.source: which is the hallmark of glassy behavior
examples.translation: yang merupakan ciri khas dari perilaku glassy
examples.suggested: yang merupakan ciri khas perilaku mirip kaca (glassy)
examples.why: Bare English adjective mid-sentence reads as unfinished translation; gloss it or render it in Indonesian.

examples.source: Optionally, use options for additional control over the submission:
examples.translation: Secara opsional, gunakan options untuk kontrol tambahan atas pengiriman:
examples.suggested: Jika perlu, gunakan opsi berikut untuk kontrol tambahan atas pengiriman job:
examples.why: 'options' is not a code identifier here; leaving it in English next to 'Secara opsional' is stiff and calqued.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and match the rest of the page: [121] says "post-processing klasik berupa **local search**", the same wording as [24]/[155], and [191] says "Suku-suku counterdiabatic ... fidelitas ground state ... perangkat keras kuantum saat ini yang masih bising", which matches [25] and [109] without adding or dropping any claim.
